VENNÉK EGY KURVANAGY DOBOZT, TELIS-TELE TIZES VILLÁSKULCCSAL! AGYIG RAKVA, TÖBB EZER. VÁGOD?

ÉS MINDENHOL, AHOL A NAP MEGFORDULOK, SZÓRNÁM SZÉJJEL, MINT A PITYPANG A SZARJAIT, VÁGOD? MINDENFELÉ!!!

scene.summary: An energetic TV reporter conducts a street interview asking a random passerby what he would do if he won the lottery jackpot. While the reporter enthusiastically suggests typical luxuries like yachts, villas, sportscars, and repeatedly 'pussy' ('pinák'), the passerby has a deeply specific and pathological fantasy: buying a giant box filled with thousands of 10mm open-end wrenches ('tízes villáskulcs') and scattering them everywhere like dandelion seeds. The passerby works himself into a terrifying, roaring rage over finding a bolt that needs a wrench, knocking the reporter flat out, before calmly walking over his body to finish his explanation. The humor lies in subverting luxurious lottery dreams with the universal, infuriating handyman trope of never finding the ubiquitous 10mm wrench when working on a car or machine.

characters.name: TV reporter
characters.description: Hyperactive street journalist carrying a microphone, wearing long pointy shoes and an unhinged wide grin. Speaks in enthusiastic TV-host banter before being completely overwhelmed and trampled.

characters.name: hooded passerby
characters.description: Bald, nonchalant man in a hoodie smoking a cigarette. Beneath his cool exterior lurks a manic, foul-mouthed DIYer/mechanic obsession driven by frustration over missing wrenches.

panels.description: The enthusiastic TV reporter speaks directly into the camera, microphone in hand, announcing they will ask a random person on the street a question.
The reporter approaches a bald man in a hoodie who is walking by while smoking a cigarette, asking him what he would do first if he won the lottery jackpot.
The passerby pauses thoughtfully to answer, while the reporter inundates him with loud guesses of clichéd lottery fantasies, obsessed with repeating 'pussy' ('pinák?').
The passerby casually flicks away his cigarette and grabs the reporter by the shoulder, enthusiastically explaining his dream of buying a huge box containing thousands of 10mm wrenches.
Gripping the nervous reporter close, the passerby gestures grandly into the distance, raving about scattering wrenches everywhere like dandelion seeds.
The passerby suddenly morphs into a monstrous, screaming demon right in the terrified reporter's face, roaring profanities about finding a bolt and needing a wrench.
The passerby calmly walks away, stepping directly on the knocked-out reporter on the ground while lighting a cigarette and concluding his monologue.

notes: Randomtibor (r0): A humorous Hungarian compound slang term meaning 'random dude' or 'random average Joe' (combining English 'random' with the common Hungarian given name Tibor).
Lottó ötös (r2, r5): The jackpot (5 matching numbers out of 90) in Hungary's classic lottery (Ötöslottó), a cultural shorthand for unimaginable wealth.

Repetitive shouting of 'PINÁK?' (r4, r8, r11): 'Pina' is vulgar Hungarian slang for cunt/pussy (used here casually to mean women/sex). The reporter constantly interjecting 'Pinák?' reflects crude, juvenile one-track thinking amidst normal luxury items.

The 10mm wrench trope (r13, r16, r17): 'Tízes villáskulcs' is a 10mm open-ended wrench. In car repair and mechanics worldwide, an M6 screw/bolt typically has a 10mm hexagonal head ('hatos csavar' refers to an M6 thread requiring a 10mm spanner). The 10mm socket/spanner is notorious among mechanics for always going missing precisely when needed most.

Slang & idioms: 'Agyig rakva' (r13) literally means 'packed up to the brain' (crammed to the brim). 'Vágod?' (r13, r15) is very common Hungarian street slang for 'you get me? / ya feel me?'. 'Szórnám széjjel, mint a pitypang a szarjait' (r15) is a colorful colloquial simile meaning 'scatter them everywhere like a dandelion scatters its seeds' (literally 'its shit').
Swear words: 'Kurvanagy' (r13) means 'fucking huge'. 'Bazmeg' (r16, r17) is Hungary's omnipresent curse word ('fuck / for fuck's sake').

r0.text: HAHA! N'ABEND! WIR WARTEN AUF DEN ERSTEN RANDOM-OTTO UND STELLEN IHM DIE FRAGE!
r0.literal: Haha! Guten Abend! Wir warten auf den ersten Random-Tibor und stellen ihm die Frage!

r2.text: TAG, DER HERR! WAS WÜRDEN SIE ALS ERSTES TUN, WENN SIE DEN JACKPOT KNACKEN?
r2.literal: Guten Tag, mein Herr! Was wäre das Erste, was Sie tun würden, wenn Sie den Fünfer im Lotto gewinnen würden?

r5.text: DEN LOTTO-JACKPOT? HM... MAL SEHEN... HEHE... JA!
r5.literal: Den Fünfer im Lotto? Hm... mal sehen... Hehe... ja!

r13.text: ICH KAUF 'NE SCHEISSGROSSE KISTE VOLL MIT 10ER-MAULSCHLÜSSELN! RANDVOLL, TAUSENDE. CHECKST DU?
r13.literal: Ich würde eine verdammt große Kiste kaufen, randvoll mit 10er-Maulschlüsseln! Bis obenhin voll, mehrere Tausend. Verstehst du?

r14.text: ICH KAUF 'NE SCHEISSGROSSE KISTE VOLL MIT 10ER-MAULSCHLÜSSELN! RANDVOLL, TAUSENDE. CHECKST DU?
r14.literal: Ich würde eine verdammt große Kiste kaufen, randvoll mit 10er-Maulschlüsseln! Bis obenhin voll, mehrere Tausend. Verstehst du?

r15.text: UND ÜBERALL, WO ICH HINGEHE, STREU ICH DIE AUS WIE DER LÖWENZAHN SEINEN SCHEISS, CHECKST DU? ÜBERALLHIN!!!
r15.literal: Und überall, wo ich mich tagsüber aufhalte, würde ich sie verstreuen wie Löwenzahn seine Scheiße, verstehst du? Überallhin!!!

r16.literal: Dass wenn da eine Sechser-Schraube ist, verdammt,

r17.text: ... EGAL WO ICH HINGREIF, EINER DA IST, VERDAMMT. NICHT EINER, FÜNF!
r17.literal: ...dann egal wo ich hingreife, einer da ist, verdammt. Nicht einer, FÜNF!
